clue.text: Precious thing to get over, competitive motoring

parts.note: gold is a precious metal, chemical symbol Au
taken as written
to cross is to get over an obstacle or road

explanation.surface: Someone describes a valuable obstacle that must be overcome in a motor race.
explanation.definitionFit: Autocross is a motor sport in which drivers race against the clock over a rough or grass course.

clue.text: Origins of cosmos explained: large-scale evolution brings a star

indicators.note: the origins of words are their opening letters, so the first letter of each following word is taken

explanation.surface: A science writer says the cosmos began in a way that produced a star.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pretends to be astronomy, so 'star' reads as a heavenly body, but it means a famous person.
explanation.definitionFit: A celeb, short for celebrity, is a famous person, the showbusiness sense of star.

clue.text: Comprehensive has charged up front for cover at night

indicators.note: says the word for charged is placed at the front, before the word for comprehensive

parts.note: something charged carries electricity, so electric
a blanket rule or ban is comprehensive, covering everything

explanation.surface: A comprehensive school is said to have charged fees in advance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Comprehensive' looks like a British state secondary school, but it is an adjective here.
explanation.definitionFit: An electric blanket is a heated bed covering used to keep warm through the night.

clue.text: Hear about wood that's cheap

indicators.note: says the word for hear goes around the word for wood

parts.note: a judge hears or tries a case in court
ash is a tree and its timber

explanation.surface: Someone listens to talk about timber that is low quality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hear' tempts you to look for a sound-alike, but it means TRY, as a court tries a case.
explanation.definitionFit: Trashy goods are cheap in the sense of shoddy, of poor quality and in poor taste.

clue.text: Wrongly name birds retreating into the distance

indicators.note: says the reversed birds go inside the word for the distance

parts.note: a mile is a unit of distance

indicators.note: says the word for birds is read backwards, as if going back

parts.note: tits are small songbirds

explanation.surface: Someone mislabels birds as they fly off into the distance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retreating' turns the birds round to give STIT, and 'into' sets that inside the distance word; the birds are not flying away.
explanation.definitionFit: To mistitle is to give something the wrong title, a wrong name.

clue.text: Two boys getting drunk a good deal?

parts.note: Roy is a boy's name
Alf is a boy's name, short for Alfred
a lush is a heavy drinker, a drunk

explanation.surface: Two lads getting tipsy on what they think is a bargain.
explanation.walkthrough: In poker a royal flush is the best possible hand, so a very good deal of the cards; the question mark flags this.
explanation.definitionFit: Poker hands are dealt, and the royal flush, ace to ten in one suit, is the top hand.

clue.text: Lolly in trifle promptly sent back

indicators.note: sent back says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone returns a sweet that was served with a dessert without delay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lolly' looks like a sweet beside the trifle, but it is British slang for money.
explanation.definitionFit: Pelf is money, especially gained dishonestly; lolly is informal British slang for cash.

clue.text: Marine mammal, close

definitions.meaning: a sea creature with flippers that breeds on land
to shut something tight, as an envelope or a deal

explanation.definitionFit: Seal names both the flippered sea animal and the act of shutting something securely.

clue.text: Royals kept wangling a way to score, of course?

definitions.text: a way to score, of course?

indicators.note: wangling means fiddling or manipulating, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The royal family kept scheming to rack up points on the golf course.
explanation.walkthrough: The course is a golf course; the question mark marks the playful definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Stroke play is a form of golf scoring where the total number of strokes over the round counts.

clue.text: Stew made with a tin full of beans

indicators.note: to stew is to cook ingredients together into a jumble, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A stew is made with a can of beans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stew' looks like the dish and 'beans' like its contents, but 'Stew' is the anagram signal and 'full of beans' the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Full of beans is an idiom for lively and energetic, which is what animated means.

clue.text: Cloakroom pin where witch secures three pretty elegant caps

indicators.note: says the word for witch holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: a hag is an ugly old woman or witch

indicators.note: the caps of words are their top letters, so the first letter of each is taken

explanation.surface: In a cloakroom a witch fastens three stylish hats on a peg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'caps' looks like hats in the cloakroom scene, but means the first letters T, P, E, which 'secures' puts inside HAG.
explanation.definitionFit: A hatpeg is a peg on which a hat is hung, the sort of fitting found in a cloakroom.

clue.text: Address on Beaumont St, Oxford curiously AE Housman's? Lumme!

indicators.note: curiously means in an odd way, so these letters are oddly rearranged

parts.note: the poet's initials and name together with the possessive S all serve as letters

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims in surprise that a famous Oxford address belongs to the poet A E Housman.
explanation.walkthrough: A E Housman was an English poet and scholar; Lumme is an old British exclamation of surprise. The Ashmolean is Oxford's art and archaeology museum on Beaumont Street.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ashmolean Museum of art and archaeology stands on Beaumont Street in central Oxford.

clue.text: Put out the litter

definitions.meaning: to publish or release something, such as a stamp or a statement
a brood of young animals born together, offspring

explanation.definitionFit: Issue means to release officially and also, in law and old usage, a person's children.

clue.text: State has run out of notes, behold!

indicators.note: says the letter for run is taken out of the word for notes

parts.note: tenners are ten-pound notes
R is the cricket abbreviation for a run
behold means look, see

explanation.surface: A country announces it has run out of banknotes, look!
explanation.walkthrough: 'notes' suggests music, but means banknotes: TENNERS, ten-pound notes, lose R to give TENNES.
explanation.definitionFit: Tennessee is one of the fifty states of the USA.

clue.text: A branch shortly becoming efficient

parts.note: a department is a branch of an organisation, abbreviated to dept

explanation.surface: A branch office will soon become efficient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' looks like 'soon', but tells you to use the abbreviation of department.
explanation.definitionFit: Being adept means being skilled and capable, so efficient at a task.

clue.text: Old film evidently has twice bombed

indicators.note: bombed means blown apart, so these letters are scattered and rearranged
says the word has is used two times

explanation.surface: A vintage movie was clearly a flop on two occasions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bombed' looks like the film flopping, but it is the anagram signal for EVIDENTLY plus HAS twice.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lady Vanishes is Alfred Hitchcock's 1938 British comedy thriller, an old film.

clue.text: Umbrella hardly opening, cry of disapproval about it

indicators.note: says the cry of disapproval goes around the first letter of hardly

parts.note: a catcall is a jeering whistle or shout of disapproval

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: An umbrella barely opens, and someone jeers at it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Umbrella' looks like the rain shield, but is used figuratively for an all-covering term.
explanation.definitionFit: An umbrella term is a catch-all, one that covers many different things.

clue.text: Poet putting love on tape

parts.note: love means zero in tennis, which looks like the letter O
vid is short for video, a recording on tape

explanation.surface: A poet records his love on videotape.
explanation.definitionFit: Ovid was a Roman poet, author of the Metamorphoses.

clue.text: Compliance in the assignment of Nautilus?

parts.note: the Nautilus is Captain Nemo's submarine in Jules Verne, and the name of the first nuclear submarine
a mission is a task one is assigned

explanation.surface: Obedience is required in the task given to a famous submarine.
explanation.walkthrough: The Nautilus is a submarine, so its assignment is a sub's mission.
explanation.definitionFit: Submission is the act of yielding or complying with another's will.

clue.text: Sly, keen to hide at the back

indicators.note: says the word for keen conceals the next piece inside itself

parts.note: to keen is to wail or cry in grief
aft means at the back of a ship

explanation.surface: A cunning person is eager to stay hidden at the rear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keen' looks like 'eager', but is the verb meaning to wail, CRY.
explanation.definitionFit: Crafty and sly are synonyms, both meaning cunning and deceitful.

clue.text: Quickly appreciate an appreciative audience?

definitions.meaning: very fast, in a British informal idiom
to enjoy the people who applaud you, read as a literal phrase

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is British slang for very fast; the second reading is contrived, taking it literally as fondness for applauders.
explanation.definitionFit: The informal British idiom means very quickly; read literally it means to be fond of those clapping.

clue.text: Insect, say, with frail wings, by houses

indicators.note: says the word by holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: to utter is to say

indicators.note: the wings of a word are its outer letters

explanation.surface: An insect with weak wings is by some houses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' looks like 'for example' after 'Insect', but is a verb; 'wings' takes the outer letters of frail, and 'houses' puts UTTERFL inside the word by.
explanation.definitionFit: A butterfly is a winged insect of the order Lepidoptera.

clue.text: Beginning to lose in battle, he's desperate for good luck!

indicators.note: desperate suggests wild and frantic, so these letters are thrown into disorder
the beginning of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Starting to lose a fight, a soldier wishes himself luck in desperation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'desperate' rearranges the start of lose with battle and he's; 'in' just places that letter among the rest before the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: All the best is a farewell wish meaning good luck to you.

clue.text: Emperor worshipped God over time in course of African trip

indicators.note: in a down clue the word for god sits over, before, the rest

parts.note: Ra is the ancient Egyptian sun god

indicators.note: says the letter for time goes into the middle of the word for African trip

parts.note: a safari is an expedition, especially in Africa

explanation.surface: An emperor revered as divine travels across Africa on an expedition.
explanation.walkthrough: Ras Tafari was the name of Haile Selassie, Emperor of Ethiopia, before his coronation; Rastafarians worship him.
explanation.definitionFit: Ras Tafari, later Emperor Haile Selassie of Ethiopia, is worshipped by Rastafarians as divine.

clue.text: Contaminate false teeth, biting article

indicators.note: says the false teeth close around the article, as teeth bite

parts.note: a denture is a set of false teeth
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Someone's false teeth bite into an item and pollute it.
explanation.definitionFit: To denature is to alter the natural character of a substance, for instance by adding something to make it unfit to drink.

clue.text: US author, books in head

indicators.note: says the books go inside the word for head

parts.note: a cape is a headland
OT is the Old Testament, a set of books

explanation.surface: An American writer has books on his mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' looks like the mind, but is a headland, CAPE.
explanation.definitionFit: Truman Capote was an American author, of In Cold Blood and Breakfast at Tiffany's.

clue.text: Fighter capsizing before me — one easily sunk?

indicators.note: capsizing means turning over, so in a down clue the word for fighter is turned upside down

parts.note: a MiG is a Russian fighter jet
taken as written

explanation.surface: A warship turns over in front of me, and is easily sent to the bottom.
explanation.walkthrough: The sinking is golf: a gimme is a putt so short it is conceded as certain to go in.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf a gimme is a putt so short it is assumed holed, so very easily sunk.

clue.text: Party to empty pub, it's suggested?

indicators.note: says the picture of an empty pub is drawn as a nought placed inside the word for pub

parts.note: an inn is a pub
nothing, nought, looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: A gathering heads for a pub with nobody in it.
explanation.walkthrough: An empty pub has nobody, nought, inside, so O goes inside INN; 'Party to' looks like a gathering but means involved in.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in on a secret or plan means being party to it, sharing knowledge of it.
